programme.title: Tonight
programme.desc: The violent murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak shocked Britain after footage of his final moments came to light at the trial of his attacker in June. Captured on the police's body-worn camera, false accusations by the aggressor against Henry, alongside his pleas to police as he lay dying, caused national uproar. In an exclusive and deeply revealing interview with ITV's Paul Brand, Henry's family share memories of a much-loved son and brother whose life was cut tragically short, while asking searching questions about the treatment he received, and the police investigation that followed. It is also the story of a family's determination to uncover the truth, secure change and ensure that Henry is remembered not for his tragic murder but for the life he lived.

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: Tonight
programme.desc: The violent murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak shocked Britain after footage of his final moments came to light at the trial of his attacker in June. Captured on the police's body-worn camera, false accusations by the aggressor against Henry, alongside his pleas to police as he lay dying, caused national uproar. In an exclusive and deeply revealing interview with ITV's Paul Brand, Henry's family share memories of a much-loved son and brother whose life was cut tragically short, while asking searching questions about the treatment he received, and the police investigation that followed. It is also the story of a family's determination to uncover the truth, secure change and ensure that Henry is remembered not for his tragic murder but for the life he lived.

programme.title: TikTok: Murder Gone Viral
programme.desc: With exclusive access to the victims' families, friends and the police, this documentary strand explores extraordinary true crime cases linked to the world's fastest-growing social media platform. In the early hours of the 11th of February 2022, two 21-year-old men - Saqib Hussain and Hashim Ijazuddin - were found dead in a burning car on the A46 in Leicestershire. Within a short time, police arrested two unlikely culprits: 22-year-old TikTok influencer Mahek Bukhari and her 45-year-old mother Ansreen. Mahek from Stoke-on-Trent has over 160,000 followers on TikTok and many millions of views - her mum Ansreen regularly appeared in her videos. Detectives discovered that Ansreen had been in a three-year-long secret relationship with Saqib Hussain which began when he was just 18 - when she wanted to end the relationship in January 2022 and Saqib threatened to send nude photos and sex tapes to her husband, Mahek hatched a plan to silence him and enlisted others into her scheme.

programme.title: Tonight
programme.desc: The violent murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak shocked Britain after footage of his final moments came to light at the trial of his attacker in June. Captured on the police's body-worn camera, false accusations by the aggressor against Henry, alongside his pleas to police as he lay dying, caused national uproar. In an exclusive and deeply revealing interview with ITV's Paul Brand, Henry's family share memories of a much-loved son and brother whose life was cut tragically short, while asking searching questions about the treatment he received, and the police investigation that followed. It is also the story of a family's determination to uncover the truth, secure change and ensure that Henry is remembered not for his tragic murder but for the life he lived.

programme.title: Deal or No Deal
programme.desc: The iconic TV series is back, but in a brand-new setting with brand-new prize boxes and a new batch of contestants hoping to win a whopping cash prize - who will have what it takes to beat our brand-new Banker? Now hosted by Stephen Mulhern, the series will see contestants battle it out against the notorious Banker to be in with a chance of winning a life-changing cash prize in a nail-biting game of nerves and intuition. Contestants are confronted with 22 sealed boxes with each one hiding a different amount of money - without knowing what each one contains, the contestant must eliminate the boxes, which are opened one at a time, and the amount of money inside is revealed. Pressure mounts as the player is tempted by the notorious Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for what might be inside their box, and as long as the larger cash prizes remain unchosen, the Banker's offers will get higher... but that can all change in an instant if a big cash prize is unveiled.

programme.title: Tonight
programme.desc: The violent murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak shocked Britain after footage of his final moments came to light at the trial of his attacker in June. Captured on the police's body-worn camera, false accusations by the aggressor against Henry, alongside his pleas to police as he lay dying, caused national uproar. In an exclusive and deeply revealing interview with ITV's Paul Brand, Henry's family share memories of a much-loved son and brother whose life was cut tragically short, while asking searching questions about the treatment he received, and the police investigation that followed. It is also the story of a family's determination to uncover the truth, secure change and ensure that Henry is remembered not for his tragic murder but for the life he lived.

programme.title: Deal or No Deal
programme.desc: The iconic TV series is back, but in a brand-new setting with brand-new prize boxes and a new batch of contestants hoping to win a whopping cash prize - who will have what it takes to beat our brand-new Banker? Now hosted by Stephen Mulhern, the series will see contestants battle it out against the notorious Banker to be in with a chance of winning a life-changing cash prize in a nail-biting game of nerves and intuition. Contestants are confronted with 22 sealed boxes with each one hiding a different amount of money - without knowing what each one contains, the contestant must eliminate the boxes, which are opened one at a time, and the amount of money inside is revealed. Pressure mounts as the player is tempted by the notorious Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for what might be inside their box, and as long as the larger cash prizes remain unchosen, the Banker's offers will get higher... but that can all change in an instant if a big cash prize is unveiled.

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: Tonight
programme.desc: The violent murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak shocked Britain after footage of his final moments came to light at the trial of his attacker in June. Captured on the police's body-worn camera, false accusations by the aggressor against Henry, alongside his pleas to police as he lay dying, caused national uproar. In an exclusive and deeply revealing interview with ITV's Paul Brand, Henry's family share memories of a much-loved son and brother whose life was cut tragically short, while asking searching questions about the treatment he received, and the police investigation that followed. It is also the story of a family's determination to uncover the truth, secure change and ensure that Henry is remembered not for his tragic murder but for the life he lived.

programme.title: Deal or No Deal
programme.desc: The iconic TV series is back, but in a brand-new setting with brand-new prize boxes and a new batch of contestants hoping to win a whopping cash prize - who will have what it takes to beat our brand-new Banker? Now hosted by Stephen Mulhern, the series will see contestants battle it out against the notorious Banker to be in with a chance of winning a life-changing cash prize in a nail-biting game of nerves and intuition. Contestants are confronted with 22 sealed boxes with each one hiding a different amount of money - without knowing what each one contains, the contestant must eliminate the boxes, which are opened one at a time, and the amount of money inside is revealed. Pressure mounts as the player is tempted by the notorious Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for what might be inside their box, and as long as the larger cash prizes remain unchosen, the Banker's offers will get higher... but that can all change in an instant if a big cash prize is unveiled.

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: Tonight
programme.desc: The violent murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak shocked Britain after footage of his final moments came to light at the trial of his attacker in June. Captured on the police's body-worn camera, false accusations by the aggressor against Henry, alongside his pleas to police as he lay dying, caused national uproar. In an exclusive and deeply revealing interview with ITV's Paul Brand, Henry's family share memories of a much-loved son and brother whose life was cut tragically short, while asking searching questions about the treatment he received, and the police investigation that followed. It is also the story of a family's determination to uncover the truth, secure change and ensure that Henry is remembered not for his tragic murder but for the life he lived.

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: Tonight
programme.desc: The violent murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak shocked Britain after footage of his final moments came to light at the trial of his attacker in June. Captured on the police's body-worn camera, false accusations by the aggressor against Henry, alongside his pleas to police as he lay dying, caused national uproar. In an exclusive and deeply revealing interview with ITV's Paul Brand, Henry's family share memories of a much-loved son and brother whose life was cut tragically short, while asking searching questions about the treatment he received, and the police investigation that followed. It is also the story of a family's determination to uncover the truth, secure change and ensure that Henry is remembered not for his tragic murder but for the life he lived.

programme.title: Deal or No Deal
programme.desc: The iconic TV series is back, but in a brand-new setting with brand-new prize boxes and a new batch of contestants hoping to win a whopping cash prize - who will have what it takes to beat our brand-new Banker? Now hosted by Stephen Mulhern, the series will see contestants battle it out against the notorious Banker to be in with a chance of winning a life-changing cash prize in a nail-biting game of nerves and intuition. Contestants are confronted with 22 sealed boxes with each one hiding a different amount of money - without knowing what each one contains, the contestant must eliminate the boxes, which are opened one at a time, and the amount of money inside is revealed. Pressure mounts as the player is tempted by the notorious Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for what might be inside their box, and as long as the larger cash prizes remain unchosen, the Banker's offers will get higher... but that can all change in an instant if a big cash prize is unveiled.

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: Tonight
programme.desc: The violent murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak shocked Britain after footage of his final moments came to light at the trial of his attacker in June. Captured on the police's body-worn camera, false accusations by the aggressor against Henry, alongside his pleas to police as he lay dying, caused national uproar. In an exclusive and deeply revealing interview with ITV's Paul Brand, Henry's family share memories of a much-loved son and brother whose life was cut tragically short, while asking searching questions about the treatment he received, and the police investigation that followed. It is also the story of a family's determination to uncover the truth, secure change and ensure that Henry is remembered not for his tragic murder but for the life he lived.

programme.title: Deal or No Deal
programme.desc: The iconic TV series is back, but in a brand-new setting with brand-new prize boxes and a new batch of contestants hoping to win a whopping cash prize - who will have what it takes to beat our brand-new Banker? Now hosted by Stephen Mulhern, the series will see contestants battle it out against the notorious Banker to be in with a chance of winning a life-changing cash prize in a nail-biting game of nerves and intuition. Contestants are confronted with 22 sealed boxes with each one hiding a different amount of money - without knowing what each one contains, the contestant must eliminate the boxes, which are opened one at a time, and the amount of money inside is revealed. Pressure mounts as the player is tempted by the notorious Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for what might be inside their box, and as long as the larger cash prizes remain unchosen, the Banker's offers will get higher... but that can all change in an instant if a big cash prize is unveiled.

programme.desc: The violent murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak shocked Britain after footage of his final moments came to light at the trial of his attacker in June. Captured on the police's body-worn camera, false accusations by the aggressor against Henry, alongside his pleas to police as he lay dying, caused national uproar. In an exclusive and deeply revealing interview with ITV's Paul Brand, Henry's family share memories of a much-loved son and brother whose life was cut tragically short, while asking searching questions about the treatment he received, and the police investigation that followed. It is also the story of a family's determination to uncover the truth, secure change and ensure that Henry is remembered not for his tragic murder but for the life he lived.

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: Tonight
programme.desc: The violent murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak shocked Britain after footage of his final moments came to light at the trial of his attacker in June. Captured on the police's body-worn camera, false accusations by the aggressor against Henry, alongside his pleas to police as he lay dying, caused national uproar. In an exclusive and deeply revealing interview with ITV's Paul Brand, Henry's family share memories of a much-loved son and brother whose life was cut tragically short, while asking searching questions about the treatment he received, and the police investigation that followed. It is also the story of a family's determination to uncover the truth, secure change and ensure that Henry is remembered not for his tragic murder but for the life he lived.

programme.title: Deal or No Deal
programme.desc: The iconic TV series is back, but in a brand-new setting with brand-new prize boxes and a new batch of contestants hoping to win a whopping cash prize - who will have what it takes to beat our brand-new Banker? Now hosted by Stephen Mulhern, the series will see contestants battle it out against the notorious Banker to be in with a chance of winning a life-changing cash prize in a nail-biting game of nerves and intuition. Contestants are confronted with 22 sealed boxes with each one hiding a different amount of money - without knowing what each one contains, the contestant must eliminate the boxes, which are opened one at a time, and the amount of money inside is revealed. Pressure mounts as the player is tempted by the notorious Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for what might be inside their box, and as long as the larger cash prizes remain unchosen, the Banker's offers will get higher... but that can all change in an instant if a big cash prize is unveiled.

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: Tonight
programme.desc: The violent murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak shocked Britain after footage of his final moments came to light at the trial of his attacker in June. Captured on the police's body-worn camera, false accusations by the aggressor against Henry, alongside his pleas to police as he lay dying, caused national uproar. In an exclusive and deeply revealing interview with ITV's Paul Brand, Henry's family share memories of a much-loved son and brother whose life was cut tragically short, while asking searching questions about the treatment he received, and the police investigation that followed. It is also the story of a family's determination to uncover the truth, secure change and ensure that Henry is remembered not for his tragic murder but for the life he lived.

programme.title: Deal or No Deal
programme.desc: The iconic TV series is back, but in a brand-new setting with brand-new prize boxes and a new batch of contestants hoping to win a whopping cash prize - who will have what it takes to beat our brand-new Banker? Now hosted by Stephen Mulhern, the series will see contestants battle it out against the notorious Banker to be in with a chance of winning a life-changing cash prize in a nail-biting game of nerves and intuition. Contestants are confronted with 22 sealed boxes with each one hiding a different amount of money - without knowing what each one contains, the contestant must eliminate the boxes, which are opened one at a time, and the amount of money inside is revealed. Pressure mounts as the player is tempted by the notorious Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for what might be inside their box, and as long as the larger cash prizes remain unchosen, the Banker's offers will get higher... but that can all change in an instant if a big cash prize is unveiled.

Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: John Nettles makes his final appearance as DCI Tom Barnaby - with his birthday approaching, Tom reluctantly accompanies his wife Joyce on a spa weekend to Swavely Manor. Seeking refuge at the village pub, Barnaby learns that Phoebe married Luke after the sudden death of her first husband and Miranda's friend Carter Smith reveals he is helping her with her novel although many in the village doubt that the book really exists - back at the spa, Luke is crushed to death by a training machine soon after being threatened by Carter. After another gruesome discovery, the truth gradually emerges - as the net closes in on the killer, all Barnaby has to worry about is his birthday party, retirement, and welcoming cousin DCI John Barnaby to Causton.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Neil Dudgeon's first appearance as the head of Causton CID. John Barnaby initially rebuffs a request from Harriet Wingate, headmistress at the upmarket Darnley Park Girls School, to patrol their forthcoming classic car show, but Barnaby is intrigued when he learns that the remains of famous racing driver Duncan Palmer have been discovered at Darnley Park 40 years after he was thought to have drowned in the Lake District. Harriet is opposed to the plans of school governor Jamie Cameron and so invites his ex-wife Kate together with her father, racing legend Peter Fossett, to the show - Fossett is annoyed that his fellow judge is club DJ Dave 'Doggy' Day, who knows nothing about cars. Soon afterwards, Doggy is crushed to death under Kate's car and Barnaby thinks the video diaries of two pupils could hold clues to the killing, but a new lead takes him to meet someone at the barn where Duncan Palmer met his death. When the killer turns on him, could Barnaby's first case also be his last?

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: DCI John Barnaby takes on another case as the head of Causton CID. A social services investigator calls on elderly eccentrics William Bingham and his wife Mary but is sent away rudely by their daughter Selina and her husband Eddie Stanton - the Binghams live as recluses in upper-class squalor while the nearby Stantons run a stud farm with Ben Viviani, who is in love with Eddie's daughter Verity. Ben's mother Maggie had also humiliated the investigator - when his body is found in a river, they therefore all come under suspicion. Mary later invites Barnaby to tea, but he discovers before he arrives that her daughter's body was never found - and then Mary is found dead. Could a mysterious reference to a moon crater called Bingham hold a clue?

programme.title: Dick Turpin

programme.title: Maigret

programme.title: Lillie

programme.title: Bellman and True
programme.desc: 1987. Thriller. Directed by Richard Loncraine. Stars Bernard Jill, Derek Newark & Richard Hope. A computer expert is forced to use his scientific genius to pull off a daring bank heist. [S]

programme.desc: 1998. Hosted by Antoine de Caunes. Tonight, we solve the secret of the moving nipple, look into the mystery of wee willy winky, watch as Lolo makes a ham sandwich and see a man getting nibbled.

programme.desc: Miss Jones sees a prowler through her window, and Rigsby suspects everyone else. A police detective appears and begins to investigate. S1 E6: The Prowler

programme.title: Rising Damp
programme.desc: An election polarises the household. Rigsby supports the Conservatives, Alan and Philip lean towards Labour, whilst Miss Jones is impressed with the Liberal candidate. S1 E7: Stand Up and Be Counted

programme.title: Rising Damp
programme.desc: Ruth is depressed following 'the deception' of a recent male friend. Rigsby takes what he believes to be his chance to woo her. S2 E1; The Permissive Society

programme.title: Rising Damp
programme.desc: With Miss Jones collecting for a famine charity, Philip challenges Rigsby to go 48 hours without eating. He gladly accepts the offer, but soon finds his will weakening. S2 E2: Food Glorious Food

programme.title: Rising Damp
programme.desc: Health and fitness are the new buzzwords in the house, and Rigsby's keenness to portray himself as in prime condition lead him to challenging Philip to a boxing match. S2 E3: A Body Like Mine

programme.title: Goodnight Sweetheart
programme.desc: Gary Sparrow is an unhappily married TV repairman who one day walks into a time warp. Nicholas Lyndhurst stars in the hit 1990s sitcom. S1 E1: Rites of Passage

programme.title: Goodnight Sweetheart
programme.desc: Gary returns to the bar to begin courting Phoebe, where he runs into her husband Donald. S1 E2: Fools Rush In

programme.title: Goodnight Sweetheart
programme.desc: Gary arouses suspicions when he saves Phoebe from an early evening bombing raid. S1 E3: Is Your Journey Really Necessary?

programme.title: On The Buses
programme.desc: Stan needs to transport Arthur and Olive's new bed to the house so he uses the 'L' bus, the passenger-free bus used to train drivers. However the bus breaks down. S4 E6: The L Bus

programme.title: On The Buses
programme.desc: Blakey takes sadistic pleasure in making Stan and Jack man the bus for the dreaded kids outing. It starts badly when Blakey accuses Stan of giving his nephew a girlie magazine. S4 E7: The Kids' Outing

programme.title: On The Buses
programme.desc: As a tenth anniversary present, Aunt Maud sends Olive and Arthur a dog, but he eats Arthur's food and gives him a sneezing allergy, so Olive takes him back on the bus. S4 E8: The Anniversary

programme.title: On The Buses
programme.desc: The chairs in the Butler house need to be re-upholstered so Stan smuggles material used for the bus seats out of the depot. All goes well until Blakey drops by. S4 E9: Cover Up

programme.title: On The Buses
programme.desc: When Stan had to apply the brakes quickly, a woman passenger falls on top of Blakey. So Blakey devises a new exit and entry system for the buses to leave and return to the depot. S4 E10: Safety First

programme.title: On The Buses
programme.desc: To make money the Butler family takes in a lodger, Mr. Nichols, the new transport manager, and of course he is given Stan's room. S4 E11: The Lodger

programme.title: Birds of a Feather

programme.title: Birds of a Feather
programme.desc: When Darryl dies, Tracey has to decide what kind of a send-off to give him. Sharon wants it to be nice for the boys and Dorien has got the perfect outfit. S12 E1: Knocking on Heaven's Door

programme.title: Birds of a Feather
programme.desc: Tracey's house has been burgled during Darryl's funeral. The family decide it's up to them to track down their possessions. S12 E2: Too Much of Nothing

programme.title: Birds of a Feather
programme.desc: Sharon's disapproval of Tracey dating policeman Barry and apparently overlooking Garth's feelings for his dad lead to a major quarrel between the sisters. S12 E3: Tombstone Blues

programme.title: Likely Lads Xmas 1974

programme.title: Tonight
programme.desc: The violent murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak shocked Britain after footage of his final moments came to light at the trial of his attacker in June. Captured on the police's body-worn camera, false accusations by the aggressor against Henry, alongside his pleas to police as he lay dying, caused national uproar. In an exclusive and deeply revealing interview with ITV's Paul Brand, Henry's family share memories of a much-loved son and brother whose life was cut tragically short, while asking searching questions about the treatment he received, and the police investigation that followed. It is also the story of a family's determination to uncover the truth, secure change and ensure that Henry is remembered not for his tragic murder but for the life he lived.

programme.title: Deal or No Deal
programme.desc: The iconic TV series is back, but in a brand-new setting with brand-new prize boxes and a new batch of contestants hoping to win a whopping cash prize - who will have what it takes to beat our brand-new Banker? Now hosted by Stephen Mulhern, the series will see contestants battle it out against the notorious Banker to be in with a chance of winning a life-changing cash prize in a nail-biting game of nerves and intuition. Contestants are confronted with 22 sealed boxes with each one hiding a different amount of money - without knowing what each one contains, the contestant must eliminate the boxes, which are opened one at a time, and the amount of money inside is revealed. Pressure mounts as the player is tempted by the notorious Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for what might be inside their box, and as long as the larger cash prizes remain unchosen, the Banker's offers will get higher... but that can all change in an instant if a big cash prize is unveiled.

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: Tonight
programme.desc: The violent murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak shocked Britain after footage of his final moments came to light at the trial of his attacker in June. Captured on the police's body-worn camera, false accusations by the aggressor against Henry, alongside his pleas to police as he lay dying, caused national uproar. In an exclusive and deeply revealing interview with ITV's Paul Brand, Henry's family share memories of a much-loved son and brother whose life was cut tragically short, while asking searching questions about the treatment he received, and the police investigation that followed. It is also the story of a family's determination to uncover the truth, secure change and ensure that Henry is remembered not for his tragic murder but for the life he lived.

programme.desc: The iconic TV series is back, but in a brand-new setting with brand-new prize boxes and a new batch of contestants hoping to win a whopping cash prize - who will have what it takes to beat our brand-new Banker? Now hosted by Stephen Mulhern, the series will see contestants battle it out against the notorious Banker to be in with a chance of winning a life-changing cash prize in a nail-biting game of nerves and intuition. Contestants are confronted with 22 sealed boxes with each one hiding a different amount of money - without knowing what each one contains, the contestant must eliminate the boxes, which are opened one at a time, and the amount of money inside is revealed. Pressure mounts as the player is tempted by the notorious Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for what might be inside their box, and as long as the larger cash prizes remain unchosen, the Banker's offers will get higher... but that can all change in an instant if a big cash prize is unveiled.
